summary: The down-zap path reaches dig.c:dighole on a magical trap. C rolls d(3,6), calls explode with TRAP_EXPLODE and EXPL_MAGICAL, then deletes the trap and redraws the map. js/dig.js records note_unported('explode.c explode') and skips the blast, so the screen and RNG diverge at segment 0 step 177. Existing js/explode.js has the source branch for TRAP_EXPLODE; the missing behavior is the dighole call and its damage roll.

source.branch: In dighole, after the too-hard guard, a magical trap triggers explode(dig_x,dig_y,0,20+d(3,6),TRAP_EXPLODE,EXPL_MAGICAL), then deltrap and newsym. The JS branch skips the roll and explosion.
callers: zap.c:weffects dispatches a digging wand or spell to zap_dig; zap.c:zap_dig calls dighole(FALSE,TRUE,NULL) for a downward zap when there are no stairs. js/zap.js:weffects -> zap_dig -> dighole already follows this path, so no caller edit is required.
dependencies: explode.c:explode is already available as js/explode.js:explode in the accepted base and handles TRAP_EXPLODE and EXPL_MAGICAL; this task only wires the existing helper from dighole.

evidence: The accepted v53 evaluation at 0ddbafd22e56dbc0365fbc0355c9dac9352cba43 records 177/206 screens and 2736/2945 RNG calls matching before the first divergence at segment 0 step 177, key >. The saved C step has rn2(19)=2 from exercise(attrib.c:509), then d(3,6)=12 from dighole(dig.c:919).

At step 177 the C topline is 'Boom! Your bolt reveals a secret door. The door absorbs your bolt!--More--'. Step 178 shows 'The lichen is caught in the magical blast! You kill the lichen!' and the explosion's damage and monster-death RNG. The JavaScript branch currently calls note_unported('explode.c explode') before deltrap and newsym, omitting the explosion path.

C source: nethack-c/upstream/src/dig.c:885-922 contains dighole's magical-trap branch; zap.c:weffects and zap_dig provide the production caller. Existing js/explode.js:410-480 sets TRAP_EXPLODE type and js/explode.js:545-590 handles its visible blast and damage path.
